question: Below what eGFR is metformin contraindicated, and where is that stated?
answer:
## Metformin is contraindicated below an eGFR of 30 mL/min/1.73 m²

This is stated in **Section 4 (Contraindications)** of the FDA prescribing information for metformin. That section lists severe renal impairment, defined as eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m², as a contraindication. [Approval Label_021574s032lbl.pdf](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/021574s032lbl.pdf)

The same label also says [Approval Label_021574s032lbl.pdf](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/021574s032lbl.pdf):
- **eGFR below 30:** stop metformin.
- **eGFR 30–45:** don't start metf

question: What does 'controlled' blood pressure mean for BPD, and where is it defined?
answer:
## What "controlled" blood pressure means for BPD

For BPD, a patient's blood pressure is controlled when their **most recent reading in the measurement year is below 140/90**. That means systolic < 140 mmHg **and** diastolic < 90 mmHg. [BPD (Blood Pressure Control)](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c460dae0-4e87-4176-bf48-c30e423c1966?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785) [BPD — Blood Pressure Control for Patients With Diabetes](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/4d584784-6771-45f2-b69f-2585bcca785d?i
